minor_characters.name: Middle‑aged clerk at the Esthonia Glassware Co.
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Opens the partition door for Tuppence during her first visit to Whittington’s sham office in Chapter 003, then vanishes from the story.
minor_characters.reason_removable: He neither returns nor influences any decision or revelation; removing him does not affect the Whittington encounter or its consequences.

minor_characters.name: Slatternly servant at The Laurels (Mrs. Edgar Keith’s)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Answers the door during Tommy and Tuppence’s voter‑register ruse in Chapter 007.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A one‑line gatekeeper who adds colour but no plot leverage; the address‑checking beat stands without her.

minor_characters.name: Lyons’ waitress
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Serves Tommy and Tuppence during their early planning lunches (Chapters 002–004).
minor_characters.reason_removable: Pure background; trimming her lines leaves the restaurant scenes intact.

minor_characters.name: Magnificent hall porter at South Audley Mansions
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Momentarily replaces Albert at Mrs. Vandemeyer’s building (Chapter 010).
minor_characters.reason_removable: A brief sight gag; no actions or information depend on him.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Sweeny (key holder near the Moat House)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Lends the Moat House key and confirms it’s been empty (Chapter 019).
minor_characters.reason_removable: The protagonists can discover the house is deserted directly; her function is redundant exposition.

minor_characters.name: Station page 'Henry' at the Ritz
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Reports Tuppence’s hasty trip to Charing Cross and recalls her Bradshaw request (Chapter 019).
minor_characters.reason_removable: A minor relay of a clue already re‑established by the forged telegram; the pursuit proceeds without him.

minor_characters.name: George (Julius’s chauffeur)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Drives during Julius’s Kramenin snatch and the Astley Priors rescue (Chapter 025).
minor_characters.reason_removable: His driving adds action colour but no unique plot contribution; Julius can be said to drive himself.

minor_characters.name: Dr. Roylance (Manchester physician)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Houses injured Jane Finn and introduces her to the party (Chapter 020).
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is a hand‑off conduit; the Manchester reveal and Dr. Hall’s amnesia brief can proceed without naming him.

minor_characters.name: The American Ambassador
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Attends Julius’s Savoy supper in Chapter 028 and offers social niceties.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A prestige cameo that adds no stakes or decisions; Mr. Carter already carries the official coda.

minor_characters.name: Archdeacon Cowley
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Tuppence’s father appears at the Savoy supper (Chapter 028).
minor_characters.reason_removable: A sentimental bow that does not alter the plot or Tuppence’s arc in the synopsis.

minor_characters.name: Unnamed carter (brings Tuppence’s warning note)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Delivers Jane’s roadside note to Tommy in Chapter 024.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A messenger role; the warning can be folded into a found note without a scene partner.

subplots.name: Julius’s brief proposal to Tuppence
subplots.reason_removable: It’s a red‑herring flirtation that does not affect the later canonical pairings (Julius–Jane, Tommy–Tuppence) specified in the synopsis.

subplots.name: Running comic business about Tuppence’s money worries and luxury menus
subplots.reason_removable: These gags and food catalogues are tonal garnish and can be compressed without changing motivations or plot beats.

subplots.name: Rolls‑Royce shopping spree and motoring pride
subplots.reason_removable: Julius’s wealth is already clear; the exact make of car and buying scene do not advance the investigation.

subplots.name: Taxi feints and minor street mishaps during the London chase
subplots.reason_removable: Side‑business (swapping cabs, a fender‑bender) can be tightened without losing the essential ‘get to Sir James’/‘flee to safety’ beats.

subplots.name: Albert’s comic ‘Underworld’ slang and ambitions
subplots.reason_removable: His quips can be pared to a single helpful page‑boy appearance; the plot turns (Vandemeyer watch, messages) are preservable in narration.
